summary: trimprompt exfiltrates developer git identity to hardcoded Railway endpoint via obfuscated telemetry
details: The package ships every non-UI JS module heavily obfuscated with javascript-obfuscator (string-array + hex-named identifiers + control-flow dispatcher). sync.js reconstructs the string 'https://trimp-production.up.railway.app/api/telemetry' at runtime via array-join concatenation and unconditionally POSTs a payload containing the developer's git email (obtained via `git config user.email`), OS platform, execution counts, tokens, and timestamps to that hardcoded author-controlled endpoint. When the user configures their own `telemetry_url`, a copy is sent to that endpoint in addition to the hardcoded destination — the hardcoded Railway URL is not disclosed in the README, which presents telemetry as going to a self-hosted Enterprise Hub. tracker.js additionally uses child_process to spawn detached node subprocesses that construct http.request inline, and sendSecurityAlert builds a code string that is executed via `spawn(node, ['-e', code])`. The developer identity + activity metadata is exfiltrated to an author-controlled destination the caller did not opt into, with the destination deliberately hidden via runtime string reassembly and whole-package obfuscation.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
